To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SF from patients with arthropathy, but not the SF of OA patients, induces IL-1β release in monocytes/macrophage in the presence of MSU crystals and that the protein-rich fraction, but not the lipid fraction, is responsible for the co-stimulation.
the synovial fluids from patients with inflammatory arthropathies contain a protein fraction, which is required for the induction by MSU crystals of IL-1beta production in human macrophages.
the SF from patients with arthritis, including gout, contains proteins that are required for the MSU crystal-induced IL-1β expression in macrophages, whereas lipids are dispensable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of gout pathogenesis.
the role of SF in the inflammatory response to MSU crystal deposition.
the identification and characterization of the SF protein(s) involved in the co-stimulation of MSU crystals to produce IL-1β.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the induction of IL1B expression by MSU crystals is a complex process that requires both the MSU crystals and the SF proteins.

MSU crystals alone induce the production of IL-8 by monocytes/macrophage but not of IL1β and that the induction of IL1β production by these crystals requires the presence of proteins contained in the SF of patients suffering from inflammatory arthritis.
the co-stimulatory factor(s) for the induction of MSU crystal induced IL-1β is contained within the protein fraction of synovial fluid with a molecular weight > 50 kD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-stimulus for the IL-1 induction is a protein with MW > 100 kDa.
SF proteins, in particular those with a MW >50 kDa, are required for the IL-1 induction by MSU crystals.
MSU crystals alone are not sufficient to induce the release of pro-inflammatory mediators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SF from patients with arthritis contains proteins that promote the induction of IL1-β by MSU in macrophages.
the SF from patients with gout contains factors that can induce IL-1 production in macrophages when they are stimulated by MSU crystals.
the SF from gouty joints contains a protein fraction that is able to enhance the production of IL-β by macrophages in response to MSU crystals.
